user.description: Enter the local IP address of your APsystems EZHI inverter. Everything below is optional. The cloud fields are only needed for the remote control entities (on/off, system mode, SOC limits) — see the README on how to obtain the tokens. For Local Control, choose the local MQTT transport and enter the smart meter's (SEM) id; the inverter and the meter have to be redirected at your MQTT broker first.
user.title: APsystems EZHI

data_description.cloud_username: Your APsystems EMA account's username, not the e-mail address. With the password it fetches the token pair and logs in again by itself when the cloud expires it.
data_description.cloud_password: The EMA account's password. Stored so the integration can log in again; leave empty if you paste tokens instead.
data_description.control_transport: How control commands reach the inverter. Local Control and the smart meter need "Local MQTT broker".
data_description.sem_device_id: The smart meter's ID: a letter followed by digits, e.g. M01234567890 (printed on the meter, shown in the vendor app). Leave empty if you have none. Needs the local MQTT transport, and the meter has to be redirected to the same broker as the inverter.
data_description.answer_ntp: Redirected to your broker, the devices ask for the time and nothing answers. Switch this on to let the integration answer, off if something else on your broker already does. Local Control works without it.

reauth_confirm.description: The cloud no longer accepts the stored token pair. Enter the username and password of your APsystems EMA account (the account username, not the e-mail address) and the integration will log in again on its own from now on — the cloud expires the token pair every seven days. A captured token pair works too, but comes back here after those seven days.
reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect APsystems cloud

error.connection_refused: Unable to connect to the inverter. Check the IP address.
error.cloud_auth_failed: The cloud rejected these credentials. Check that you copied both tokens correctly.
error.invalid_auth: The EMA cloud rejected that username and password. Note that it wants the account username, not the e-mail address.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the EMA cloud. Try again in a moment.
error.incomplete_credentials: Enter both the username and the password, or neither.
error.missing_credentials: Enter the account username and password, or a token pair.
error.invalid_sem_id: That is not a device id. The meter's id is a letter followed by digits (printed on the SEM and shown in the vendor app), without spaces or slashes.
error.sem_needs_local_mqtt: Local Control works through the local MQTT broker. Choose the local MQTT transport as well, or clear the meter id.
error.ntp_needs_local_mqtt: Answering time requests only applies to devices redirected to the local broker. Choose the local MQTT transport as well, or switch this off.
error.mqtt_not_configured: Home Assistant has no MQTT broker configured, so the local MQTT transport has nothing to talk through. Set up the MQTT integration first.
error.mqtt_device_unknown: The inverter's id is not known, so the broker connection cannot be checked. Keep "Check connection during setup" on while the inverter is reachable, or set the transport in the options once the integration has polled the inverter.
error.mqtt_no_reply: The broker is there, but the inverter did not answer over it. It has not been redirected at your broker — see the integration's local-control documentation.
error.sem_no_reply: The inverter answers over the broker, but the smart meter did not. It has not been redirected at your broker, or the id is wrong -- see the Local Control documentation.

device_options.description: Polling intervals for the local API, and the optional cloud credentials. Enter your APsystems EMA username and password to fetch the tokens automatically — the username, not the e-mail address. They are stored so the integration can log in again when the cloud expires the token pair, which it does every seven days. Local Control: with the local MQTT transport, enter the smart meter's (SEM) id to let the inverter regulate to it by itself -- it adds a switch, an offset and the meter's readings. The meter has to be redirected at the same broker as the inverter.
